criteria_verification.notes: Password configuration correctly reads GUARDKIT_NATS_PASSWORD from environment (or optional env_file). Raises ValueError with actionable message for missing/blank password. Tests verify both cases.

NATSConfig constructed with exact parameters: url='nats://127.0.0.1:4222', user='guardkit', password=SecretStr, name='guardkit-harvest'. NATSClient created with source_id='guardkit-harvest'. Tests verify all parameters.
Publish lifecycle correctly implements: await client.connect() → loop over episodes calling await client.publish_episode(ep) → await client.disconnect(). Uses disconnect() not close() as specified.

Per-episode ValueError handling implemented. Oversized episodes (>900 KB) caught per episode, recorded in skipped_oversized count, logged with episode_id/size/'chunk upstream' message. Loop continues after skip - one oversized doc does not abort run.
Idempotent/resumable design confirmed. No client-side deduplication state. Relies on deterministic episode_id → Nats-Msg-Id for JetStream dedupe. Re-running publishes same ids.
All NATS operations delegated to NATSClient.publish_episode(). No hand-rolled subject construction, header setting, or direct NATS client calls. publish_episode owns all NATS protocol details.
Returns PublishResult dataclass containing: published (int), skipped_oversized (int), counts_per_type (dict[str, int]). Result populated during publish loop.

Based on available evidence (Player report, requirements checker, orchestrator test execution), unit tests use AsyncMock(spec=NATSClient) with no live broker. Tests verify connect/publish/disconnect ordering, oversized episode handling, and run continuation. 14 tests reported passing. However, independent test verification layer did not complete (see critical issue above).
Code compiles successfully with py_compile. Follows PEP 8 conventions with proper type hints, docstrings, organized imports (stdlib/third-party/local), and error handling.
